$comment: The events module's register. events/tools/fetch.py reads this file; events/AGENTS.md explains the fields. An id here is the `source` value on every event the calendar contributes, and the prefix of that event's `id`.

sources.name: Illuminate
sources.note: The City of Awe's free-concert calendar. One iCal feed carries the upcoming slate — but no per-event URL, so entries link the public `page` where they are listed. LOCATION is a street address with no venue name, so venues.json does the naming. WordPress robots.txt disallows nothing relevant.

sources.name: SF Rec & Park
sources.note:
CivicPlus. Each calendar in the issue's CID list has its own iCalendar feed at common/modules/iCalendar/iCalendar.aspx?catID=&feed=calendar; several are empty by design. LOCATION is 'Venue - address' text, occasionally wrapped in

tags. robots.txt disallows /RSS.aspx and /map.aspx but not calendar.aspx or the iCalendar feed.

sources.name: Nature in the City
sources.note: Squarespace events collection; ?format=json lists `upcoming` with title, startDate/endDate (ms epoch) and a location object whose mapLat/mapLng are real when set and the Squarespace default (40.7207559, -74.0007613) when not. The /calendar page is an empty shell — the collection is /events.

sources.name: Alemany Farm
sources.note: No feed: the workshops page is hand-maintained WordPress markup — each workshop is an <h3>, a <strong> line with the date and hours, and an Eventbrite register button. All events are at the farm. robots.txt allows everything but asks Crawl-Delay: 20 — one request per run.

sources.name: Friends of Sunset Dunes
sources.note: Squarespace events collection like natureinthecity's. Same NYC-default coordinate sentinel to drop. Venues are usually entrances along the park ('Sunset Dunes @ Irving'); the addressTitle names the spot.
